note: No animal has PNH and eculizumab binds only human C5, so the class was built on an in-vitro complement hemolysis assay (sensitized chicken erythrocytes in human serum), murine surrogate-antibody toxicology, and the human genetics of inherited C5 deficiency for infection risk.
label: PNH (anti-C5)

engagement.model: In-vitro complement hemolysis assay (sensitized chicken erythrocytes in human serum)
engagement.note: Humanized h5G1.1 (eculizumab) blocked complement lysis of chicken erythrocytes in human serum; no patient data yet.
engagement.short: h5G1.1 blocks complement lysis in vitro
engagement.quote: Finally, an intact humanized h5G1.1 antibody blocked human complement lytic activity at concentrations identical to the original murine monoclonal antibody.

engagement.model: In-vitro complement hemolysis assay (sensitized chicken erythrocytes in human serum)
engagement.note: In 11 PNH patients, complement-sensitive type III erythrocytes rose from 36.7% to 59.2%: terminal complement attack blocked as the assay predicted.
engagement.short: PNH type III cells survive in patients
engagement.quote: The mean percentage of PNH type III erythrocytes increased from 36.7 percent of the total erythrocyte population to 59.2 percent (P=0.005).
engagement.reason: PNH cells survive; complement blocked in patients
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level reading of a paywalled NEJM paper; it reports the patient side only, so the comparison is mine. The FDA 2007 clinical pharmacology review ran the same chicken-RBC assay on dosed patients' serum ('complete inhibition of hemolytic activity was achieved in almost all patients who received an eculizumab dose of 2.0 mg/kg or higher') while cautioning that 'it is unknown whether this ex vivo assay correlates with in vivo hemolytic response in patients with PNH'. Nishimura 2014 (doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1311084) later showed the assay also explains non-engagement: C5 p.Arg885His is not bound by eculizumab in vitro and its 11 carriers among 345 Japanese patients did not respond.

dose.model: In-vitro complement hemolysis assay (blocking concentration in human serum)
dose.note: Assay set the exposure logic: complete blockade needs antibody in molar excess of serum C5, so dosing targets a trough above that threshold.
dose.quote: The humanized Fab and scFv molecules blocked complement-mediated lysis of chicken erythrocytes and porcine aortic endothelial cells in a dose-dependent fashion, with complete complement inhibition occurring at a three-fold molar excess, relative to the human C5 concentration.

dose.model: In-vitro complement hemolysis assay (blocking concentration in human serum)
dose.note: Same assay ex vivo put complete blockade at 29–55 µg/mL; PNH troughs held ~100 µg/mL and LDH fell from week 1.
dose.short: Troughs above assay threshold suppressed LDH
dose.quote: It was also seen that these levels resulted in immediate (Week 1) and sustained lowering of serum LDH, a marker for intravascular hemolysis (Figure 1).
dose.reason: Troughs above assay threshold suppressed LDH
dose.judgement: Source is a scanned FDA review read by OCR (macOS Vision); the quoted passage read cleanly but is subject to OCR fidelity. 'These levels' are the preceding sentence's troughs: 'above 40 mcg/mL ... sustained at approximately 100 mcg/mL'; the review's Emax fit gives E50 ~43 mcg/mL and the ex vivo complete-inhibition range in single-dose RA/SLE patients was 29–55 mcg/mL, which it calls 'rough estimates'. Magnitude is direction-only because the in-vitro assay yields a stoichiometric threshold (molar excess over C5), not a dose. Breakthrough hemolysis at sub-threshold troughs, and ravulizumab's later free-C5 <0.5 mcg/mL target (current DailyMed label), are consistent with the model. Crovalimab/SKY59 added cynomolgus C5 pharmacology (Fukuzawa 2017, doi 10.1038/s41598-017-01087-7); eculizumab could not, having no cross-reactive species. Registry: NCT00122330 (C04-001/TRIUMPH) has no results posted.

efficacy.model: In-vitro complement hemolysis assay (no animal model of PNH)
efficacy.note: No animal has PNH; the class inferred efficacy from the Ham-test logic that PNH red cells die by terminal complement, blockable in vitro.
efficacy.short: No PNH animal; in-vitro lysis assay only
efficacy.quote: These results demonstrate that humanized h5G1.1 and its recombinant derivatives retain both the affinity and blocking functions of the murine 5G1.1 antibody, and suggest that these molecules may serve as potent inhibitors of complement-mediated pathology in human inflammatory diseases.

efficacy.model: In-vitro complement hemolysis assay (no animal model of PNH)
efficacy.note: Pilot in 11 patients: LDH fell 3111→594 IU/L, transfusions 2.1→0.6 units/month, hemoglobinuria −96%; TRIUMPH 2006 confirmed (LDH AUC −85.8%).
efficacy.short: LDH and transfusions fell as predicted
efficacy.quote: Mean lactate dehydrogenase levels decreased from 3111 IU per liter before treatment to 594 IU per liter during treatment (P=0.002).
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level (paywalled NEJM); TRIUMPH (Hillmen 2006, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa061648, NCT00122330, no registry results) is the randomized confirmation. No disease model existed, so the prediction scored is the mechanistic one (block C5, stop lysis of PNH cells) and it held for intravascular hemolysis. Two un-modelled residuals are not scored as contradictions: C3-opsonised PNH cells undergo extravascular hemolysis on treatment (Risitano 2009, doi 10.1182/blood-2008-11-189944), and C5 p.Arg885His carriers do not respond (Nishimura 2014), which the same in-vitro assay reproduces. No anti-C5 antibody has a published failed PNH trial, so `neg` is unavailable.

safety.model: Inherited human C5 deficiency (natural genetic model); no cross-reactive animal species
safety.note: Risk reasoned from humans with inherited C5 deficiency before any patient was dosed; trials vaccinated first and excluded hereditary complement deficiency.
safety.short: Neisseria risk predicted from C5-deficient humans
safety.quote: Eculizumab is safe and well tolerated in patients with PNH.
safety.judgement: Opener only. The pre-dosing vaccination design is stated for the pivotal studies in the 2007 label ('Patients received meningococcal vaccination prior to receipt of Soliris') and the registry records NCT00122330/NCT00122304 (both started 2004) exclude 'Hereditary complement deficiency' and 'History of meningococcal disease', i.e. the C5-deficiency logic written into eligibility; I could not quote the pilot's own vaccination sentence (abstract only).

safety.model: Inherited human C5 deficiency (natural genetic model); mouse surrogate-antibody toxicology
safety.note: Meningococcal sepsis in 2/196 vaccinated trial patients, as C5-deficiency biology predicted; mouse surrogate-antibody toxicology (no cross-reactive species) was silent on infection.
safety.quote: In clinical studies, 2 out of 196 PNH patients developed serious meningococcal infections while receiving treatment with Soliris; both had been vaccinated.
safety.reason: Predicted infection risk confirmed in patients
safety.judgement: Status rests on the model the class actually relied on for infection risk, human terminal-complement-deficiency genetics, not on the animal package: the FDA pharmacology review (125166s0000_PharmR.pdf, OCR) found eculizumab 'did not inhibit hemolysis in the non-primate and primate sera, indicating that eculizumab was only specific to human complement C5', so toxicology used the murine surrogate BB5.1 in mice (silent on Neisseria) and PK/PD used human-C5-reconstituted C5-deficient mice; product_in_model is therefore false. Scored `same` not `contra` because the prediction was made and acted on (vaccination, boxed warning) before and at approval. Post-marketing CDC surveillance found 16 US cases in 2008–2016, 14 vaccinated, a 1,000–2,000-fold incidence (McNamara 2017, doi 10.15585/mmwr.mm6627e1): vaccination does not remove the risk, which the current label now states. The label gives cases, not the genetic inference, so comparison_stated is false.
